headline: Still no dip: BTC $84.3k holds as 5.17% 10-year and Bitget restart loom Monday
summary: As of 23:30 UTC on Saturday 26 September there is still no live dip in any of the three: BTC is $84,252.90 against an $84,090.50 open (+0.19%) in a tight $83,777.00-$84,401.90 range, ETH $2,688.05 (-0.12%) in a $2,663.17-$2,697.17 range, and SOL $121.10 (-0.84%) after the flush to $119.84 was bought back, leaving the week at +3.8% BTC, +2.2% ETH and +9.8% SOL. The Hormuz standoff has not escalated in the last five hours - Trump's rejection of Iran's seven-day reopening plan stands, he says the US has 'total control' with 29 ships crossing in 24 hours, and foreign minister Araqchi says Tehran is still waiting for a definitive US position through mediators rather than retaliating - so the tail risk is unresolved but dormant going into the Sunday futures reopen. The real bid remains institutional but is thinning: US spot bitcoin ETFs took about $2.39bn in the week to 25 September, the biggest of 2026, flipping year-to-date flows to roughly +$934m from -$5.8bn in mid-July, yet daily inflows decayed from $999m on 21 September to $134m on the 25th. Positioning is not crowded: Hyperliquid funding is a benign 0.00084%/h on BTC and 0.00125%/h on ETH and SOL, BTC and SOL futures trade at a discount to spot (-0.038% and -0.021%), open interest is $3.10bn / $2.96bn / $684m, and only 53 items came through in 24 hours. Fear & Greed is 74 and the composite 63.0, both Greed, so the mood is confident while the danger sits in the calendar, not the tape: Bitget restarts withdrawals at 08:00 UTC Monday, the 10-year closed Friday at 5.17% after touching a 19-year high of 5.23%, and PCE, ISM and payrolls all land before 2 October.

BTC.note: $84,252.90, up 0.19% on the session inside a 0.74%-wide $83,777.00-$84,401.90 range with $3.10bn of open interest, funding at 0.00084%/h and futures 0.038% below spot - no dip trigger at all, and for context the history file records 92.9% of 28 stored BTC dips recovering +1.5% within 14 days (median 5.0 h, 78.6% inside 24 h) and 100% of the 7 that fired during greed.

ETH.note: $2,688.05, effectively unchanged (-0.12%) in a $2,663.17-$2,697.17 range and still the laggard at +2.2% on the week against SOL's +9.8%, with $2.96bn of open interest and a futures premium of only 0.007%; the file's 91 stored ETH dips recovered +1.5% within 14 days 92.3% of the time, 92.9% of the 28 that occurred during greed.

SOL.note: $121.10, off 0.84% from a $122.12 open and the only one with real range - the drop to $119.84 was bought straight back - after the strongest week of the three at +9.8%, on $684m of open interest with funding flat at 0.00125%/h and futures 0.021% below spot, which reads as give-back after a rally rather than distribution; 93.9% of 132 stored SOL dips recovered within 14 days, median 3.5 h.

drivers.title: Hormuz standoff unresolved but quiet: Trump's rejection stands, Iran still awaiting a formal US answer
drivers.detail: Trump on 26 September rejected Iran's proposal - delivered through mediators - to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and restart peace talks within seven days in exchange for lifting the US naval blockade, saying 'I'm rejecting their deal, that deal would not be acceptable', that the US has 'total control' of the waterway with 29 ships crossing in the past day, and that Iran 'outsmarted themselves' and 'don't have any money now'. Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araqchi has since said Tehran has not yet received an official US response and will decide once Washington's definitive position is conveyed; Saudi Arabia called for international action to protect freedom of navigation, and no new strikes or tanker incidents have been reported in the last several hours. Tehran still insists on the right to levy transit fees, so nothing is settled - this is the most likely source of a Sunday-night gap.

drivers.title: 10-year closed at 5.17% after a 19-year high of 5.23%, with ~70% priced for another October hike
drivers.detail: The US 10-year Treasury yield touched 5.23% on Thursday 24 September, the highest in 19 years, and closed Friday at 5.17%, after the FOMC delivered its first increase in three years to a 3.75%-4.00% target range; markets now price roughly 70% odds of a further 25bp at the 27-28 October meeting, and 16 of 19 FOMC members project at least one more hike this year. Kevin Warsh's 'the Committee will deliver price stability' line is credited with moving October odds from 43% to 64% inside a month. CoinDesk noted on 25 September that bond volatility surged while bitcoin and Wall Street stayed calm - crypto is simply not pricing this, so if the adjustment comes it arrives as a gap rather than a grind.

drivers.title: The ETF bid is real but fading day by day
drivers.detail: US spot bitcoin ETFs took about $2.39bn in the week to 25 September, the largest weekly total of 2026 and the biggest since October 2025, across seven consecutive inflow days worth roughly $2.8-3.0bn; that flipped year-to-date flows positive at about +$934m after a $5.8bn deficit in mid-July. The shape of it is the new information: daily inflows fell from $999m on Monday 21 September to $191m on Thursday and $134m on Friday, which reads more like a rebound from the summer selloff being bought than the start of fresh demand. Ether ETFs have seen outflows in most months of 2026 and the summer money returning to bitcoin largely skipped ETH, which is consistent with ETH being the weakest of the three on the week.

drivers.title: Bitget puts the breach at $387.5m and publishes a staged withdrawal restart from Monday 08:00 UTC
drivers.detail: Bitget froze withdrawals on 24 September and now puts unauthorised transfers at about $387.5m, up from an initial $351.6m once Zcash and TRON assets were counted. Bitcoin withdrawals reopen at 08:00 UTC on 28 September, ETH (plus BNB Chain, Arbitrum, Base, Optimism) on the 29th, USDT (Ethereum, BNB Chain, Solana, Tron) on the 30th, and other tokens, fiat and P2P on 2 October; the team says the vulnerability is patched and Mandiant and SlowMist are running independent checks. Against that, the attacker moved roughly $83m of stolen XRP on 26 September that Ripple has no ability to freeze, and Circle and Tether had only caught 218,023 USDT and 99,990 USDC. Bitget says its protection fund covers the loss, so this is a confidence risk rather than a solvency one - but a queue that stalls on Monday is the clearest single route to a panic candle this week.

drivers.title: US-China truce extended to 10 January, removing the November tariff cliff
drivers.detail: Xi Jinping's three-day Washington state visit ended Friday 25 September with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent confirming the trade truce due to expire in November is extended to 10 January, a two-month rollover of the Busan deal that lowered US tariffs and suspended Beijing's rare-earth and critical-minerals export controls. The White House fact sheet frames it as a 'fair and reciprocal relationship'; in substance the visit produced pageantry and few concrete agreements, and the two sides did not agree on AI. For crypto this matters mainly as a removed catalyst - one of the scheduled macro shocks that could have hit in November has been pushed into 2027's first quarter.

drivers.title: Solana's outperformance has its own drivers: Alpenglow on a second testnet, $32.8m of ETF inflow
drivers.detail: Solana's Alpenglow upgrade, which replaces Proof of History and Tower BFT to target 150-millisecond finality, reached its second public test network on 26 September, and US spot Solana ETFs took $32.81m in a single session, lifting cumulative assets to about $1.81bn. SOL futures open interest has grown roughly 14% from early September to about $7.49bn, and the token first traded above $120 on 25 September for the first time since 29 January. That explains why SOL is +9.8% on the week against BTC's +3.8% - and why its $684m of Hyperliquid open interest and 0.00125%/h funding are worth watching: it is the most extended of the three, so it is the most likely to produce a real dip if the tape turns.

watch.what: Oil and index futures reopen for the week. This is the first price to react to Trump's rejection of Iran's Hormuz roadmap and to Araqchi's 'awaiting a definitive US position' reply. A gap up in crude pushes the 10-year off 5.17% and is the most plausible route to a genuine crypto dip inside 48 hours; a quiet open leaves the range intact.

Bitget restarts Bitcoin withdrawals, the first stage of a queue that runs through 2 October. A queue that clears quietly removes the last acute crypto-specific risk; a delay, a third revision to the $387.5m figure or visible outflows from other exchanges is the clearest candidate for a flush.
RBA decision, US JOLTS job openings for August, and Fed speakers Goolsbee and Williams - the first read on whether the October hike stays at ~70% priced.

US PCE price index for August plus final Q2 GDP, alongside German, French and Italian inflation and China's NBS manufacturing PMI. With an October hike ~70% priced and the 10-year at a 19-year high, a firm core PCE is the most direct scheduled pressure on crypto's range.
US ISM manufacturing PMI for September and jobless claims, plus the Japan Tankan survey - the warm-up to payrolls and the check on whether last week's unusually strong US composite PMI was a one-off.

September nonfarm payrolls, with eurozone flash HICP the same morning. A hot print into a Fed already priced to hike again is the cleanest macro path to a dip. The same day is SEC Commissioner Hester Peirce's last - the commission's steadiest crypto advocate - and the DoubleZero token unlock.

Iranian retaliation risk while Tehran waits on the formal US answer, and the Hormuz transit-fee demand it has not dropped. Watch for tanker incidents, a resumption of US strikes, or new Treasury sanctions on Iranian crypto networks, all of which have moved BTC before.
FOMC decision closing the 27-28 October meeting, roughly 70% priced for a further 25bp on top of the 3.75%-4.00% target range set last week.
